items.prompt: You can climb 1 or 2 stairs at a time. How many distinct ways are there to reach stair n?
items.why: The last move came from n−1 or n−2, so ways(n) = ways(n−1) + ways(n−2), with no budget dimension. Different orders of steps are different ways, which is why it isn't the unbounded-knapsack combination count.

items.prompt: Houses stand in a row with some money in each. You can't rob two neighbours. Maximise the loot.
items.why: best(i) = max(best(i−1), best(i−2) + money[i]) only looks back two positions. It looks like take/skip knapsack, but there's no capacity. Greedy (richest house first) fails on [2, 1, 1, 2].

items.prompt: Count the ways to make an amount from unlimited coins of given values, where {1, 2} and {2, 1} count once.
items.why: Order doesn't matter → count combinations: unbounded knapsack with the coins in the outer loop. A Fibonacci-style recurrence over the amount alone would count every order separately.

items.prompt: A message of digits is encoded with 1 → A … 26 → Z. Count the ways to decode it.
items.why: The last letter used either the last digit or the last two digits, so ways(i) = ways(i−1) [if valid] + ways(i−2) [if valid]: a two-step look-back over one position. You count the decodings, you don't list them, so backtracking is overkill.

items.prompt: Given an array of positive numbers, decide whether some of them (each at most once) sum exactly to S.
items.why: The state needs a budget (the remaining sum) as well as the position, and each number is used at most once → 0/1 knapsack. Fibonacci-style DP only has the position.

items.prompt: Given a string, find the length of its longest palindromic subsequence.
items.why: The state is a range [i..j] of the string, a 2-D interval DP, not a single position looking back a fixed few steps.

items.prompt: Count the ways to write n as an ordered sum of 1, 3 and 4.
items.why: Ordered sums: the last term is 1, 3 or 4, so f(n) = f(n−1) + f(n−3) + f(n−4). That's a staircase with steps {1, 3, 4}. Unbounded knapsack would count each multiset once.
